text:
Diego: hey team, first day here (revenue infra). Trying to follow the quickstart but `kubectl` keeps pointing to a different cluster and I can't access the `fraud` namespace. Any tips? :slightly_smiling_face:

Diego: here's what I ran:
```
$ kubectl config current-context
aws-dev-us-east-1
$ kubectl get pods -n fraud
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User \"okta|diego@redwood.com\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"fraud\"
```

Lina: welcome Diego :wave: two quick things: make sure your kubeconfig was merged with `~/.kube/config` from the onboarding bundle and that your Okta groups synced. Also run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n fraud` to confirm.

Diego: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n fraud` -> returns `no`. I downloaded the kubeconfig from the starter doc and merged it using `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:./kubeconfig kubectl config view --merge > /tmp/merged && mv /tmp/merged ~/.kube/config`

devex-bot: Hi Diego! For new hires we default to ephemeral viewer access for 7 days. Use the onboarding form: https://intranet.redwood.com/onboarding/kube-access. Include namespace=fraud, access=view, ttl=7d, manager. The request auto-creates a ticket and notifies infra-oncall. If you need immediate read-only access, tag @infra-oncall here.

infra-oncall: @Diego quick option: I can create a RoleBinding that maps the `view` ClusterRole to your Okta principal in `fraud`. Before I do that, please run:
```
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n fraud --as=system:serviceaccount:infra:readonly-onboard
# expected: yes
```
If that returns yes, I'll mirror it to you. Otherwise we need the ticket to investigate group sync or the kubeconfig's user field.

Diego: ran impersonation check -> returns yes. Posted the form, ticket TB-3492.

infra-oncall: applied `rolebinding/fraud-onboard-diego` with `view` to `okta|diego@redwood.com`. Should be immediate. Also confirmed your context is fine (aws-dev-us-east-1) and maps to the right cluster.

Sam: FYI if anyone else hits merge issues, prefer `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` after setting KUBECONFIG env to avoid duplicate contexts.

Diego: can now list pods!
```
$ kubectl get pods -n fraud
NAME                         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
fraud-detector-6c7b4        1/1     Running   0          5d
alert-processor-ff9bd       2/2     Running   0          2d
```
Thanks all, excited to be here :tada:

Lina: welcome aboard! ping me if you want `edit` later after code walkthrough.
